I understand — getting three cards to fail at once is scary. Here are the most likely explanations and what you can do right now.

Why all three might decline
- Different per-card ATM limits:
  - Teen (Light Green) accounts often have a low ATM limit (example: $150/day). If your daughter tried more than that it would decline.
  - Blue accounts have a higher ATM limit (example: $500/day). If you tried $550 on Blue or Green and the card’s limit is below that, it will be declined.
- Card-specific limits vs. ATM limits: some ATMs or ATM networks impose their own per-transaction limits lower than your bank’s limit — switching machines can help.
- Velocity/anti-fraud protections: multiple declined attempts in quick succession (especially across multiple cards) can trigger automatic velocity blocks or other temporary security holds. Those blocks may apply per card, and if several cards on the same family or linked profile show suspicious patterns, each can be affected.
- Parental controls on the teen card: teen/light accounts have parental restrictions that can block ATM/withdrawal types or amounts.
- Simultaneous terminal or network issue: a local network or ATM problem can cause declines for many cards at the same machine or area.
- Available balance / no-overdraft rules: if any account doesn’t have sufficient available funds, ATM withdrawals will be declined.
